rationale: Start with a broad scouting gradient that spans almost the full solvent range at a moderate slope and temperature, so we can see where the 10 compounds elute and whether any are unretained or still retained at 42 min. This first run should map the usable phi window and indicate whether later optimization should focus on narrowing the gradient, changing steepness, or adjusting temperature for selectivity.

All 10 peaks are fully resolved, so the only score loss is from t_last = 12.64 min; the next step is to shorten the run while keeping the elution window focused around the observed peak region. A narrower, steeper gradient should pull the last peak earlier, and the current excess resolution margin gives room to trade some resolution for speed.

We have already reached the maximum CRF, so this run probes whether an even shorter, tighter gradient can preserve full resolution while maintaining t_last under 10 min. The current weakest pair still has some margin, so a modest increase in steepness is the most efficient way to test robustness and possibly shorten cycle time further.

The compressed method showed the limiting pair is 6/7, so the next informative move is a small temperature change rather than more slope changes, since close pairs with similar slope response often need selectivity tuning. Keeping the proven 12 min gradient while raising T slightly tests whether that pair can be improved without pushing the last peak beyond 10 min.

The +5 C shift strongly worsened the critical 6/7 pair, showing that temperature changes this selectivity; the most informative opposite test is 35 C on the otherwise optimal method. This checks whether cooling improves that pair while likely still keeping the last peak near or under 10 min.

The 12 min, 40 C method is already optimal by CRF, but the critical pair sits close to the threshold, and both hotter and colder runs hurt selectivity. A slight lengthening at 40 C should improve the narrow mid-run cluster's resolution with minimal risk to the time term, testing robustness around the current optimum.

Since 12 min at 40 C is already perfect, the most useful remaining test is whether lowering phi0 slightly can restore margin for the early critical cluster without sacrificing the sub-10 min last peak. This broadens the low-phi portion where peaks 5-7 appear to separate, while keeping phi1 and tG fixed to preserve overall timing.

We now have two perfect methods; this test keeps the lower phi0 that preserved the critical pair while raising phi1 slightly to try to pull the last peak a bit earlier. It checks whether we can improve speed margin below 10 min without over-compressing the mid-run cluster.

Raising phi1 compressed the critical 6/7 pair, so the complementary test is to lower phi1 while keeping the successful low phi0. This should slightly ease the gradient in the region where the limiting pair elutes and show whether extra selectivity margin can be gained while staying near the 10 min threshold.

The trends show phi1 controls the time/resolution tradeoff while lower phi0 mainly adds retention to the whole window; to map the other edge of the sweet spot, test the higher-phi version starting from phi0 0.15. This checks whether a slightly more aggressive window can keep all pairs at or above 1.5 while reducing the safety margin on t_last less than the 0.10→0.80 method did.

A 12 min gradient is perfect at both phi0 values, while 10 min at higher phi0 was just too steep for the 6/7 pair; lowering phi0 should ease the effective slope through the critical cluster while keeping the last peak well below 10 min. This directly tests whether we can gain a shorter robust method without changing temperature, which previously hurt selectivity.

The only unresolved question around the optimum is whether a smaller temperature shift than ±5 C can improve the limiting selectivity, since 45 C and 35 C moved the bad overlap to opposite neighboring pairs. Testing 30 C on the proven gradient explores that trend further and may separate the central cluster differently while keeping the last peak close to the 10 min limit.

Temperature excursions clearly disrupt selectivity, so stay at 40 C and probe the lower-phi0 branch with a slightly longer gradient. Since 0.10→0.75 at 12 min is perfect but right on the threshold and 10 min is too steep, 14 min should reveal whether this window gives a more robust separation margin than the 0.15→0.75 method, even if it likely costs some time term.

The low-phi0 branch remains promising, and 0.10→0.75 at 12 min is also perfect; lowering phi0 one more step tests whether the critical mid-run pair gains extra selectivity from a gentler effective gradient in the early-to-middle region. This is a focused check of robustness versus the current best methods while keeping the same proven tG and temperature.

The optimum appears centered near phi1 0.75 and tG 12 at 40 C, with the critical pair very sensitive to gradient steepness; testing a higher phi0 at the same endpoint isolates the effect of a narrower window from the low-phi side. This should show whether modestly trimming early weak retention can improve time without losing the 6/7 pair completely, completing the phi0 trend around the best method.

To complete the slope/window map near the optimum, test a 10 min method with the proven central phi window shifted slightly gentler at the high end than the failed 0.20→0.70 run. This asks whether a shorter method can recover enough resolution for the 6/7 pair by combining the successful phi0 0.15 setting with the lower phi1 that previously improved separation at longer tG.

The remaining unexplored corner near the optimum is the narrower, higher-organic window at the same 12 min and 40 C. This will complete the phi0/phi1 neighborhood map and test whether a more shifted window can still hold the critical 6/7 pair at full credit while giving a faster last peak.

The data show a smooth loss of the 6/7 resolution as phi1 rises from 0.75 to 0.80, but mapping one more step clarifies how steep that deterioration is and confirms the optimum sits below this region. This is mainly a boundary check on the high-phi end of the successful 12 min, 40 C family.

With the optimum region already identified, one remaining useful check is how much extra robustness the same selectivity window gains from a still shallower slope. This will define the resolution/time tradeoff curve beyond 14 min for the best window and confirm that the perfect 12 min method really is the shortest fully resolved option.

At 40 C, short steep methods mainly fail at the 6/7 pair, and temperature clearly changes that selectivity strongly; a different window may let a hotter run reorder or open that pair while keeping the last peak very early. This is a targeted interaction test of T with the lower-phi1, short-gradient regime rather than the already mapped 0.75 endpoint family.

To finish mapping the short-gradient edge at 40 C, lower phi0 one step while keeping the 10 min, phi1 0.70 program. This should soften the effective gradient where the critical 6/7 pair elutes and tests whether the faster family can be rescued without the temperature changes that consistently harmed selectivity.

One remaining informative corner is whether the lower phi1 window can tolerate the temperature increase better than the 0.75 and 10 min families did, since phi1 0.70 at 40 C improved the critical pair at the cost of some time. This interaction test may reveal whether the poor 45 C result was specific to the 0.75 endpoint rather than temperature universally.

The 6/7 pair consistently improves as the gradient is made gentler, but t_last crosses 10 min by phi1 0.70; lowering phi0 helped retain the time penalty somewhat on that branch. Testing 0.10→0.65 at 12 min checks whether a narrower, lower-end window can keep all peaks in-gradient and strengthen the critical pair enough to offset the expected later last peak.

The best region is clearly around 12 min and 40 C, with phi0 and phi1 trading time against the critical 6/7 pair; one useful untested point is the low-phi0, high-phi1 corner. This checks whether combining the slower start that helped resolution with the stronger end that shortens the last peak can still achieve full credit, potentially defining the broadest robust plateau around the optimum.

The optimum is already established at 0.15→0.75, 12 min, 40 C, but one final untested point on the same branch can complete the high-phi1 boundary and confirm how sharply the critical 6/7 pair collapses as the endpoint rises. This last run is a clean edge-mapping experiment around the proven best family.
